auth.token_source: Admin settings > Provisioning > Generate new token
auth.notes: Only one SCIM token is valid at a time; generating a new token invalidates the previous one.

operations.notes: Coda's SSO article says managed provisioning can create, update, import, deactivate, reactivate and delete users; the SCIM and IdP articles list only create, update, deactivate and group push, so delete is left null.

deprovision.data_retained: Docs are kept and can be transferred to a new owner; untransferred docs stay editable for 7 days, then become read-only until transferred. Reactivated users regain their previous doc access.
deprovision.notes: frees_seat comes from the Admin API description of user deactivation ("ensuring the user is no longer paid"); the SCIM docs do not restate it.

attributes.notes: Coda does not publish a SCIM attribute list. Entra's tutorial maps userName, active, name.givenName and name.familyName; JumpCloud's page maps further attributes; both are IdP pages, see idp_apps.

limitations.text: SAML SSO must be configured before SCIM can be turned on.
For Microsoft Entra ID, Coda tells admins not to use the Entra gallery app (it does not support sharing with groups) and to create a custom app instead.
Deactivating SCIM-provisioned users in Coda is discouraged; the Admin API rejects activation changes when SCIM is enabled unless bypassScim is set.

scim.notes: The SCIM Base URL is shown in Admin settings > Provisioning; its pattern is not published. SCIM version 2.0 comes from JumpCloud's Coda page.

auth.notes: Org-admin API token from coda.io/account, sent as a Bearer token.

capabilities.notes: Groups are read-only (list groups and members as provisioned by SCIM). Roles are per workspace (Admin, DocMaker, Editor). create_user is false: workspace add only takes an existing user.

endpoints.purpose: Deactivate a user (no longer paid; docs can be reassigned)
Transfer docs and workspace membership from a deactivated user
Add an existing user to a workspace with a role
Remove a user from a workspace (not from the org)

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhooks deliver audit events (which include user login/logout and role changes); no separate user-lifecycle event list is published.

rate_limits.text: Unspecified per-minute limit; HTTP 429 when exceeded. List endpoints take limit 1-500 (default 100) with pageToken paging.

limitations.text: Admin API cannot create users or manage group membership; groups come only from SCIM.

user_api.notes: The Admin API is separate from the public Coda (doc) API, which is open to all users but only covers docs, tables and pages, not user management.

okta.notes: Okta lists SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate and Group Push. Coda calls it the Coda-built Okta connector.

entra.notes: Gallery app provisions users, but Coda says it is outdated and recommends a custom non-gallery app for group sharing.

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud page says create, update, deactivate users; it also says groups are not supported while Coda documents JumpCloud group push.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google sign-in on all plans (login only, no provisioning); a one-time Google Groups import via Okta is documented.

row.evidence: The Superhuman Docs (formerly Coda) pricing page lists "SAML SSO" and "Provision users via SCIM" only under the Custom-priced Enterprise plan, and Coda's help centre says "SCIM is only available to customers on our Enterprise plan".
row.notes: Coda now sells as Superhuman Docs; coda.io/pricing redirects to superhuman.com/plans/docs. Prices changed since June: Pro is now $12/Doc Maker/mo annual ($15 monthly; was $10/$12), and the Team tier is now Business at $33/Doc Maker/mo annual ($40 monthly; was Team $30). Only Doc Makers are billed; editors and viewers are free. SAML SSO, SCIM (users and group push) and the Admin API (users, groups, audit events) are Enterprise-only, Contact Sales. SAML must be configured before SCIM. Coda built the Okta connector; for Entra, Coda tells admins to use a custom (non-gallery) app because the gallery app does not support group sharing.

conflicts.text: JumpCloud's Coda page lists Group Push but also says groups are not supported; Coda's own docs describe pushing JumpCloud groups.
Coda's SSO article says SCIM can delete users; the SCIM setup article lists only create, update, deactivate and group push.

open_questions: SCIM base URL pattern, token expiry, filtering, pagination and full attribute list are not published by Coda.
Whether SCIM deprovisioning ends active sessions is not documented.
Whether SCIM delete is supported (SSO article says yes, SCIM article omits it).
No Google Workspace or OneLogin catalogue app with provisioning found; OneLogin page not checked (blocks bots).
